target: A televisão está na sala.
english: The TV is in the living room.
tip: Nouns ending in -ão are usually masculine: o avião, o coração, o limão. But some are feminine: a mão, a televisão, a estação.

target: O que você faz da vida?
english: What do you do for a living?
tip: 'O que' means 'what.' 'Fazer da vida' is the natural way to ask about someone's profession in Brazil.

target: Como se diz isso em português?
english: How do you say this in Portuguese?
tip: 'Como' means 'how.' 'Como se diz' is the impersonal way to ask – literally 'how does one say.'

target: Por que não vamos à praia?
english: Why don't we go to the beach?
tip: 'Por que não' = why don't we. 'Vamos à praia' – 'à' is the contraction of 'a + a' (to the, feminine).

target: O que você acha dessa ideia?
english: What do you think of this idea?
tip: 'O que você acha de' is the go-to phrase for asking opinions in Brazilian Portuguese. Much more common than 'o que você pensa.'

target: Como se escreve o seu sobrenome?
english: How do you spell your last name?
tip: 'Como se escreve' = how does one write/spell. Very useful when filling out forms or making reservations.

target: As praias do Nordeste são maravilhosas.
english: The beaches of the Northeast are wonderful.
tip: 'As praias' – feminine plural. 'Do Nordeste' = de + o = of the Northeast. 'Nordeste' is masculine.

target: Uma amiga minha trabalha nesse banco.
english: A friend of mine works at this bank.
tip: 'Nesse' is the contraction of 'em + esse' (in this). Other contractions: neste (em + este), naquele (em + aquele), nisso (em + isso).

target: Ela tem uma amiga que mora no Japão.
english: She has a friend who lives in Japan.
tip: 'Uma amiga' – indefinite feminine article. 'Amigo' (masc.) / 'Amiga' (fem.) – the ending changes with gender.

target: O filme foi tão bom quanto o livro.
english: The movie was as good as the book.
tip: 'Tão + adjective + quanto' means 'as... as': 'tão bom quanto' = as good as. You can also use 'como' instead of 'quanto.'

target: Ela mora numa casa com um jardim grande.
english: She lives in a house with a big garden.
tip: 'Numa' is the contraction of 'em + uma' (in a, feminine). 'Num' = 'em + um' (masculine). Very common in speech.

target: Estou procurando a estação de trem, pode me ajudar?
english: I'm looking for the train station, can you help me?
tip: Regular -ar verbs in the preterite: the eu form ends in -ei, the ele/ela form ends in -ou.

target: Preciso ir ao correio mandar uma encomenda.
english: I need to go to the post office to send a package.
tip: 'Ao correio' = a + o = to the (post office). 'Correio' is masculine. 'Uma encomenda' – feminine.

target: Nós preferimos comida caseira.
english: We prefer homemade food.
tip: 'Comida caseira' means homemade food. In Brazil, homemade food is highly valued – 'comida de verdade' (real food) is a common expression.

target: Eu gosto das músicas brasileiras.
english: I like Brazilian songs.
tip: 'Das músicas' = de + as = of the (feminine plural). Contraction of preposition + article is mandatory.

target: A mão dele está machucada.
english: His hand is injured.
tip: 'Mão' is one of the few -ão nouns that is feminine: a mão. Its plural is 'as mãos.'

target: O sistema do computador travou.
english: The computer system froze.
tip: 'Sistema' is masculine (o sistema) despite ending in -a. Words of Greek origin ending in -ma are usually masculine: o tema, o cinema, o diploma.

target: Vocês precisam de alguma coisa?
english: Do you need anything?
tip: 'Precisar de' in questions: 'Vocês precisam de alguma coisa?' 'Alguma coisa' = something/anything.

target: Eu prefiro água com gás.
english: I prefer sparkling water.
tip: Unlike Spanish 'gustar,' Portuguese 'gostar' works normally: 'eu gosto de música' (I like music) – subject is the person.

target: Ela gosta de tirar fotos.
english: She likes taking photos.
tip: Different from Spanish `gustar` (which flips the subject). Portuguese `gostar` works straightforwardly: subject + gostar + de + thing.

target: Vocês gostam de comida picante?
english: Do you like spicy food?
tip: Question with 'gostar de': the 'de' stays even in questions. 'Comida picante' = spicy food.

target: Ele prefere café sem açúcar.
english: He prefers coffee without sugar.
tip: 'Preferir' doesn't need a preposition – just 'prefiro café' or 'prefiro ir a pé.' Unlike 'gostar de' and 'precisar de.'

target: O tempo está horrível hoje.
english: The weather is terrible today.
tip: 'Horrível' = horrible/awful. Adjectives ending in -vel are the same for masculine and feminine.

target: Eu trabalhei até tarde ontem.
english: I worked until late yesterday.
tip: Regular -ar past: trabalhar → trabalhei (eu). First person: drop -ar, add -ei.

target: As flores do jardim estão lindas.
english: The garden flowers are beautiful.
tip: 'As flores' – feminine plural article 'as.' Most nouns ending in -a are feminine: flor is an exception (ends in -r but is feminine).

target: O problema do trânsito é sério.
english: The traffic problem is serious.
tip: 'Do' is the contraction of 'de + o' (of the, masculine). These contractions are mandatory – you can never say 'de o.'

target: As ruas do centro estão cheias.
english: The downtown streets are crowded.
tip: 'estão' (estar) – marks a temporary condition, emotion, or location. Ser would imply permanence.

target: As escadas do prédio são íngremes.
english: The building stairs are steep.
tip: 'é' (ser) – for permanent qualities, identity, origin. Using estar would imply a temporary state.

target: A voz dela é muito bonita.
english: Her voice is very beautiful.
tip: 'Dele/dela' = his/her. More specific than 'seu/sua' which can mean his/her/your.

target: Nós saímos cedo do trabalho ontem.
english: We left work early yesterday.
tip: Regular -ir verbs in the past: -i, -iu, -imos, -iram. 'Sair' → 'saí' (eu), 'saiu' (ele/ela).

target: Eu paguei a conta do restaurante.
english: I paid the restaurant bill.
tip: Regular -ar past: pagar → paguei. Spelling change: g → gu before -ei (like ligar → liguei).

target: A mochila da minha filha é rosa.
english: My daughter's backpack is pink.
tip: 'A mochila' – feminine. Most nouns ending in -a are feminine. 'Da' = de + a (of the).

target: A foto do perfil dela é bonita.
english: Her profile picture is pretty.
tip: 'Foto' is feminine (a foto) because it's short for 'fotografia.' Similarly, 'moto' is feminine (a moto) from 'motocicleta.'

target: Tem um gato no telhado.
english: There's a cat on the roof.
tip: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'tem' is commonly used to mean 'there is/there are,' even though formal grammar prefers 'há.'

target: Eu comprei um presente para ela.
english: I bought a gift for her.
tip: 'Um' is the masculine indefinite article (a/an). 'Uma' is the feminine: um livro, uma mesa.

target: Os sapatos estão debaixo da cama.
english: The shoes are under the bed.
tip: 'Os sapatos' – masculine plural. 'Debaixo da cama' = under the bed. 'Da' = de + a.

target: Ela não gosta de acordar cedo.
english: She doesn't like waking up early.
tip: 'Gostar de' + infinitive for activities: 'não gosta de acordar.' The 'de' is always required before the verb.

target: O café está quente e forte.
english: The coffee is hot and strong.
tip: Adjectives ending in -e don't change for gender: quente is the same for masculine and feminine. Only number changes: quentes.

target: O quarto é pequeno, mas aconchegante.
english: The room is small but cozy.
tip: 'Aconchegante' means cozy/warm/inviting. It's an adjective ending in -e, so it doesn't change for gender: o quarto aconchegante, a casa aconchegante.

target: O suco está gelado e refrescante.
english: The juice is cold and refreshing.
tip: Key contractions: de+o=do, de+a=da, em+o=no, em+a=na, a+o=ao, a+a=à – you must use these, never write 'de o' separately.

target: Eu emprestei dinheiro para um amigo.
english: I lent money to a friend.
tip: 'Emprestar' in Brazilian Portuguese means both 'to lend' and 'to borrow.' Context clarifies: 'emprestei para ele' = I lent to him. 'Emprestei DELE' = I borrowed from him.

target: O filho da vizinha é muito educado.
english: The neighbor's son is very polite.
tip: `-inho` softens tone: `um momentinho` (just a sec), `obrigadinho` (thanks, friendly). Not about size – about warmth.

target: As férias dos funcionários são em janeiro.
english: The employees' vacations are in January.
tip: 'Férias' is always plural in Portuguese – there's no singular form. 'As férias' = vacation(s).

target: Eu preciso de mais tempo para terminar.
english: I need more time to finish.
tip: 'Precisar de' = to need (something). Like 'gostar de,' the preposition 'de' is mandatory: 'preciso de mais tempo.'

target: Ela escolheu o restaurante para o jantar.
english: She chose the restaurant for dinner.
tip: Verbs ending in -car, -gar, -çar have spelling changes in 1st person preterite: fiquei, paguei, comecei – to preserve pronunciation.

target: A cor da parede combina com os móveis.
english: The wall color matches the furniture.
tip: 'Cor' is feminine: a cor. Some nouns don't follow the -o/-a pattern and must be memorized.

target: Nós jantamos num restaurante italiano.
english: We had dinner at an Italian restaurant.
tip: Regular -ar past: jantar → jantamos. Same form as present – context ('num restaurante italiano') clarifies past.

target: Os meninos estão brincando no quintal.
english: The boys are playing in the backyard.
tip: 'Os meninos' – masculine plural article 'os.' Nouns ending in -o are usually masculine: menino → os meninos.

target: Ela vai à academia todo dia.
english: She goes to the gym every day.
tip: 'À' is the contraction of 'a + a' (to the, feminine). This is the famous 'crase' – it gets its own accent mark in Portuguese.

target: O atendimento nesse hotel é excelente.
english: The service at this hotel is excellent.
tip: 'Em' contracts with demonstratives: em + esse = nesse, em + aquele = naquele – always use the fused form.

target: A chave da porta está na gaveta.
english: The door key is in the drawer.
tip: 'Da' is the contraction of 'de + a' (of the, feminine). 'Da porta' = of the door.

target: O problema é a falta de tempo.
english: The problem is the lack of time.
tip: 'Problema' is masculine (o problema) despite ending in -a. This is one of the most common gender mistakes learners make.

target: O caminho até a praia é bonito.
english: The way to the beach is pretty.
tip: 'caminho' – diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Ele gosta de acordar cedo para correr.
english: He likes waking up early to run.
tip: Portuguese `gostar` always takes `de`: `gosto de pizza`, `gosto de você`. Drop the `de` and the sentence breaks. English `like` has no preposition; Portuguese needs one.

target: Os pratos da comida mineira são fartos.
english: The dishes of Minas Gerais cuisine are generous.
tip: 'são' (ser) – for permanent qualities, identity, origin. Using estar would imply a temporary state.

target: O hotel é simples, mas limpo e confortável.
english: The hotel is simple but clean and comfortable.
tip: 'Com' contracts with pronouns: comigo (with me), contigo (with you), consigo (with himself/herself/yourself formal).

target: Minha mãe é a mulher mais forte que eu conheço.
english: My mom is the strongest woman I know.
tip: 'Per' + 'o' gives 'pelo' – distinct from 'por + o' which also gives 'pelo'. Both mean 'by/through the'.

target: Ele gastou muito dinheiro na reforma.
english: He spent a lot of money on the renovation.
tip: Regular -ar past: gastar → gastou. 'Gastar' = to spend (money). 'Na reforma' = on the renovation.

target: Meu irmão mais novo é o mais alto da família.
english: My younger brother is the tallest in the family.
tip: 'Mais novo' = younger, 'mais alto' = tallest/taller. 'O mais + adjective + da' = the most...of (superlative).

target: Eles são muito barulhentos.
english: They're very noisy.
tip: Contractions extend to demonstratives: de+este=deste, em+aquele=naquele, a+aquela=àquela. These are mandatory in all registers.
